summary:
ROUND 7, TESTS. PASS, no findings. The four confirmations asked for all hold, each measured in my own tree from the staged bytes (sha256 of the staged blob equals sha256 of the file I mutated: test 8ccbf4d6..., gate 24a2d505...).

(1) THE TEST FILE'S EXECUTABLE CONTENT IS UNCHANGED, proven against the round-6 object rather than against a packet. Blob c6eac6a (the round-6 staged blob, still reachable in the object store) diffed against `git show :buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ArchiveRowSizeTest.java` yields exactly one hunk, lines 17-19 -> 17-20, entirely inside the class-level /** ... */ block that opens at line 13 and closes at line 34. No import, no field, no helper, no @Test, no assertion differs. File length 242 -> 243. The gate's delta is likewise one comment line ('of the 121 rows in the archive are already over this cap' -> 'of the 121 rows already in the BASE are over this cap'), inside a leading `#` block.

(2) THE SUITE IS GREEN from the staged bytes: `./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks` BUILD SUCCESSFUL; ArchiveRowSizeTest tests=5 skipped=0 failures=0 errors=0; across all buildSrc classes tests=269 failures=0 errors=0.

(3) THE REVISED JAVADOC PARAGRAPH IS TRUE OF THE TESTS AND OF THE TREE, recomputed from scratch with the gate's own ROW recogniser rather than carried forward. Over HEAD:backlog-done.md (which IS the base the gate reads: the script does `git show '%s:%s' % (base, archive)` with base = CHECK_RANGE or 'HEAD'): 121 matched rows, 121 distinct ids, median 1306, maximum 18845 and it is the M0.56 row, 25 rows over the 4000 cap, second largest 11481 (M4.9) -- so 'an earlier draft said 11,481, the SECOND largest, and gave the count as 120, the archive minus exactly the row it had missed' is arithmetically consistent. check-session-load.sh's header does carry 18,845 (line 9, 'the longest single row was 18,845'). THE NEW CLAUSE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED AND IT IS TRUE: over the STAGED archive the same recogniser counts 122, so 'a ref that moves as this commit lands would say 122' is exact, and the old wording {@code HEAD:backlog-done.md} would have gone stale the moment the commit landed -- 121 is a property of the BASE, which is what the sentence now says. I also confirmed the gate judges this commit's own row rather than exempting it: M0.76 is absent from HEAD:backlog-done.md, the new row is 973 characters, and the gate prints 'ok 1 new archive row(s) ... 0 already in the base and exempt'.

(4) NO KILL FROM THE ROUND-6 BATTERY IS LOST. I re-ran 15 mutants, one Gradle run each, against the staged gate. KILLED (11): CAP 4000 -> 999999; `n > cap` -> `n >= cap`; ROW narrowed to check-session-load.sh's strict `^\| (M\d+(\.\d+)+) \|`; the ID exemption dropped (`in known` -> False); exemption computed by BYTES instead of by id; the exemption TEST done by bytes; CHECK_RANGE ignored (rng = ''); `sys.exit(failed)` -> `sys.exit(0)`; `base = rng` -> `base = 'HEAD'`; `n = len(body)` -> `n = len(line)` (the '+' off-by-one); the bash `[ $? -eq 0 ] || FAILED=1` propagation deleted. SURVIVED (4), and they are exactly and only the set already filed as M0.78: the fail-closed diff guard alone, the fail-closed base guard alone, `judged += 1` deleted, and `judged` incremented for EXEMPT rows. The gate was byte-restored after every mutant and verified identical at the end. So the comment-only edits changed no kill and created no survivor.

ONE MEASUREMENT CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROUND-6 RECORD, offered for M0.78 rather than as a finding, because the survivor FAMILY is already filed and the remedy is unchanged. M0.78's notes say 'Replacing the diff with the worktree file survives'. Measured on both readings: replacing `git diff --cached -U0` with a WORKTREE DIFF (`git diff -U0 HEAD`) does SURVIVE, for the stated reason -- every test writes and stages in one call, so ADDED-LINES-ONLY is pinned by nothing. But reading the worktree FILE wholesale, in either or both branches, is KILLED, by withACheckRangeTheGateJudgesTheRangeRatherThanTheEmptyIndex, whose first case commits an over-cap row and then asserts the staged reading is silent -- the worktree still holds that row. Dropping the ADDED-LINES filter entirely is also KILLED, by anOverCapRowThatAlreadyShippedStaysEditable... at line 170. So M0.78's precise open mutant is the worktree DIFF, not the worktree FILE; the fix it prescribes (stage separately from writing) closes it either way.

ON MY ROUND-6 MINOR (the suite scratches in the system temp directory, testing.md:74 rule 17): I AGREE IT SHOULD BE DEFERRED, and it is better placed than 'needs its own row' suggests -- the row already EXISTS and resolves. M0.33 in the open backlog is 'Pin java.io.tmpdir under build/tmp for buildSrc's test task (testing.md rule 17)', and it already names the cause I measured independently: binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts pins it for the eight product modules, but buildSrc is a separate Gradle build (rootProject.name = "build-conventions") that never applies that plugin. So no new row is needed, this commit must not carry the fix (it moves every buildSrc suite at once), and the finding is not re-raised here. It never constrained anything: every mutant above behaves identically whether the scratch repositories land in /tmp or in build/tmp.

NOTHING WAS WEAKENED. No existing test file is touched by this commit -- ArchiveRowSizeTest.java is the only test in the staged set and it is an addition -- so there is no assertion whose looseness could be tracking a production change.
